title: Cleanup after reading
statement: Let $x$ be a finite Boolean input and let $c$ be a configuration with $m$ work tapes. Suppose $r$ and $s$ are distinct tape indices and the head on tape $r$ is at position $0$. For any natural number $k\le |x|$, valid input-head position $ip$, and optional Boolean value $a$, there is a number $T$ such that the reading program, started in phase $rw_1(a)$ with tape $s$ holding the binary representation of $k$ and input-head position $ip$, reaches the terminal state corresponding to $a$, with input-head position $1$ and tape $s$'s head at position $0$. Every configuration at a time $n<T$ lies in the read frame of $c$.
hypotheses_covered: A finite Boolean input $x$ and a configuration $c$
